sources.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
sources.locator: §2.1 pp.120–124 (mesh and linear/general subdivision); §2.C pp.177–179 through proof of 2C.1; Appendix p.520 Proposition A.1

contents.name: 2C.1 proof, p.178; direct closed-cover verification — adapted subclaim: Finite simplicial weak topology agrees with euclidean topology
contents.support: For finite K, the weak topology is the Euclidean subspace topology in R^{V(K)}; in particular it is compact metric and Hausdorff.

contents.name: 2.C, p.178, star paragraph and Lemma 2C.2 — adapted subclaim: Open and closed stars in a subdivision
contents.support: The open vertex star consists of points with positive coordinate at that vertex; the closed star is the subcomplex of faces of simplices containing it. Apply this separately to K and sd K.

contents.name: Appendix Proposition A.1, p.520 — adapted subclaim: Compact subsets of an arbitrary simplicial realization meet finitely many open simplices
contents.support: Assuming the Axiom of Countable Choice, every compact subset of |K| meets finitely many open simplices and is contained in a finite subcomplex, with no local-finiteness assumption. In particular a finite family of continuous maps from compact simplices has image in one finite subcomplex.

contents.name: 2.1, p.121, cone identity adapted to oriented simplicial chains — adapted subclaim: An augmented simplicial cone has an explicit chain contraction
contents.locator: 2.1, p.121, cone identity adapted to oriented simplicial chains
contents.support: If K is a simplicial cone with specified apex a, its augmented integral complex contracts by h[v0,...,vn]=[a,v0,...,vn], with repeated vertices interpreted as zero and h[-1](1)=[a].

contents.name: 2.1, pp.121–122, recursive subdivision — adapted subclaim: Oriented simplicial subdivision chain map
contents.support: The graded subdivision operator S:C_n(K;Z)->C_n(sd K;Z) sends each oriented simplex to its consistently oriented top-dimensional subdivided simplices, S_0[v]=[{v}].

contents.name: 2.1, pp.121–122 — adapted subclaim: Oriented simplicial subdivision commutes with boundary
contents.support: dS=Sd on the augmented complex, hence also on ordinary chains.

contents.name: 2.1, p.120 (complete mesh argument); Maunder 2.5.15 p.53 — adapted subclaim: Mesh of iterated simplicial barycentric subdivision tends to zero
contents.support: If finite Euclidean K has dimension n>=1, simplex mesh(sd^r K)<= (n/(n+1))^r mesh(K); every vertex star has diameter at most twice simplex mesh. Empty and zero-dimensional complexes have mesh zero.

contents.name: 2C.1 and 2C.2 proofs, pp.178–179 — adapted subclaim: The open star criterion produces a simplicial map
contents.support: For finite K, continuous f:|K|->|L| and vertices g(v) with f(st(v)) subset st(g(v)), g extends simplicially. f(x) and |g|(x) lie in the carrier simplex of f(x); straight-line interpolation is continuous, fixed where they agree, and respects every given subcomplex pair mapped by f.

contents.name: 2C.1 pp.177–179; Maunder 2.5.4 p.47 — adapted subclaim: Finite simplicial approximation for maps of pairs
contents.support: For finite K, A subset K and B subset L, every continuous f:(|K|,|A|)->(|L|,|B|) has a simplicial approximation g:(sd^r K,sd^r A)->(L,B) for all sufficiently large r, homotopic as a map of pairs to f b_K^r.

contents.name: 2.1 pp.121–122 — adapted subclaim: The subdivision chain of an oriented two simplex
contents.support: Compute S[a,b,c] and its boundary explicitly, preserving orientation.

contents.name: Proposition A.1 p.520, simplicial specialization — adapted subclaim: A compact set in an infinite non locally finite realization still meets finitely many cells
contents.support: In the weak realization of countably many edges sharing a vertex, any compact subset lies in finitely many edges, although the common vertex is not locally finite.

contents.name: General singular chains, small chains, telescoping homotopy and excision
contents.reason: These singular-chain constructions are later consumers; importing them here would reverse the repair dependency.

sources.reading_status: complete for the declared range: full proofs read for geometric/chain subdivision pp.120–123 and simplicial approximation pp.177–179; Appendix A.1 consulted for weak topology

sources.title: C. R. F. Maunder, Algebraic Topology
sources.locator: §2.5, Definitions 2.5.1–2.5.20 and their proofs, pp.45–56; §4.3 Theorem 4.3.9 and discussion after 4.3.10 pp.119–120; additional continuation pp.56–57 consulted

contents.name: 2.5.10, pp.51–52 (face-chain description) — adapted subclaim: Face poset and order complex
contents.support: The face poset consists of nonempty faces ordered by inclusion. For a poset P, its order complex has vertices P and finite totally ordered subsets as faces, including the empty face.

contents.name: 2.5.7–2.5.10, pp.49–52 — adapted subclaim: Barycentric subdivision of an abstract simplicial complex
contents.support: sd K is the order complex of the nonempty face poset of K; sd of a subcomplex is a subcomplex.

contents.name: 2.5.7–2.5.10, pp.49–52 — adapted subclaim: Canonical barycentric realization map
contents.support: b_K sends vertex sigma to |sigma|^{-1} times the sum of its vertices, and extends affinely on chains.

contents.name: 2.5.8 and 2.5.10, pp.49–52 — adapted subclaim: Barycentric face chains triangulate a geometric simplex
contents.support: The barycenters of each strict face chain are affinely independent, and their simplices triangulate the original simplex, with precisely common-chain-face intersections.

contents.name: 2.5.8, pp.49–50; weak-topology extension proved locally — adapted subclaim: Barycentric subdivision realizes homeomorphically
contents.support: For every abstract K with weak realization topology, b_K:|sd K| -> |K| is a homeomorphism, compatible with all subcomplex inclusions.

contents.name: 4.3.9 proof, p.119, carried induction; specialized cone version — adapted subclaim: Simplicial chain maps carried by specified cones are chain homotopic
contents.locator: 4.3.9 proof, p.119, carried induction; specialized cone version
contents.support: Let each simplex sigma of K be assigned a cone subcomplex Phi(sigma) of L with specified contraction, nested under faces. Any two augmentation-preserving chain maps carried by Phi are joined by a carried chain homotopy.

contents.name: 2.5.13, p.52, vertex-selection approximation — adapted subclaim: Last vertex map is carried by original simplices
contents.support: For a specified total order on V(K), lambda:sd K->K sends a nonempty face to its greatest vertex. It is simplicial and carried by original faces.

contents.name: 4.3.9 and subdivision discussion following 4.3.10, pp.119–120 — adapted subclaim: Simplicial subdivision is a chain map and homology isomorphism
contents.support: S is a chain-homotopy equivalence on integral ordinary and augmented chains. Its inverse up to homotopy is lambda_#. Consequently subdivision preserves ordinary homology and the local augmented reduced convention, including degree -1.

contents.name: 2.5.7–2.5.8 pp.49–50 — adapted subclaim: Relative derived subdivision of a finite simplicial pair
contents.support: For finite A subset K define D_A K by leaving A unchanged and, in increasing dimension, coning each subdivided boundary of a simplex outside A from its barycenter. Iterate with A fixed.

contents.name: 2.5.10–2.5.12 pp.51–52 — adapted subclaim: Relative derived subdivision makes the fixed subcomplex full
contents.support: After one relative derived subdivision A is full: each simplex meets |A| in a face or the empty set; later relative derived subdivisions preserve this.

contents.name: 2.5.18–2.5.20 pp.54–56; Zeeman theorem proof pp.40–42 — adapted subclaim: Relative subdivision neighbourhood adjustment
contents.support: For finite A subset K, a further subdivision near A admits a piecewise affine h:|K|->|K| homotopic to id rel |A|, sending a neighbourhood of A into A. Off that neighbourhood the remaining vertex stars shrink under sufficiently many relative subdivisions; near A their h-images are subordinate to vertex stars of A.

contents.name: 2.5.7–2.5.9 pp.49–51 — adapted subclaim: Barycentric subdivision of an edge and triangle
contents.support: An edge subdivides into two edges; a triangle into six triangles indexed by maximal nonempty face chains.

contents.name: 2.5.1–2.5.6 pp.46–48 — adapted subclaim: A continuous map need not be simplicial before subdivision
contents.support: A continuous self-map of an edge can fail to be simplicial in the original triangulation.

2.5.6 Nonuniqueness and failure of an approximation before subdivision
2.5.9 Worked relative subdivision of three triangles

sources.title: E. C. Zeeman, Relative simplicial approximation (1964)
sources.locator: Complete article pp.39–43, theorem, addendum, corollary, fullness lemma, proofs and counterexample

contents.name: Theorem and proof, pp.39–42; Maunder 2.5.20 pp.55–56 — adapted subclaim: Relative simplicial approximation after subdivision
contents.locator: Theorem and proof, pp.39–42; Maunder 2.5.20 pp.55–56
contents.support: Let K,L be finite complexes, A subset K, and f:|K|->|L| continuous with f|A simplicial. For some r there is g:D_A^r K->L with |g|=f on |A| and |g| homotopic to f rel |A|. Thus it is a homotopy of pairs (K,A)->(L,f(A)). A preassigned compatible linear subdivision on A can be extended before applying this assertion.

contents.name: Relative theorem pp.39–42, interval specialization — adapted subclaim: A relative simplicial approximation fixed on the endpoints
contents.support: For f:[0,1]->[0,1], f(x)=x^2, a simplicial map after midpoint subdivision can be homotopic to f rel both endpoints.

contents.name: Opening warning pp.39–40; elementary vertex obstruction — adapted subclaim: Ordinary barycentric subdivision cannot fix a nonconstant simplicial edge
contents.locator: Opening warning pp.39–40; elementary vertex obstruction
contents.support: If the fixed subcomplex contains an edge mapped identically to an unsubdivided target edge, a simplicial map from sd^r K to that target cannot agree pointwise there for r>=1.

contents.name: Relative theorem and neighbourhood adjustment proof
Fullness lemma
Addendum: neighbourhood-controlled homotopy
contents.reason: The fixed-subcomplex conclusion is retained in full; arbitrary prescribed-neighbourhood control is an additional geometric approximation estimate.

contents.reason: This requires a target refinement and quantitative closeness formulation beyond the assigned finite simplicial-pair conclusion.

sources.title: C. P. Rourke and B. J. Sanderson, Introduction to Piecewise-Linear Topology
sources.locator: Chapter 2 pp.13–16: cells, complexes, subdivisions, 2.6–2.12; Appendix to Chapter 2 pp.27–30 (Lemmas A/B, four corollaries and proof of 2.7)

contents.name: Chapter 2, Cells and Cell Complexes, pp.13–15 — adapted subclaim: Finite convex cell complex and linear subdivision
contents.locator: Chapter 2, Cells and Cell Complexes, pp.13–15
contents.support: A finite convex cell complex in Euclidean space consists of compact convex polyhedral cells, includes their faces and the empty cell, and intersections are common faces. A linear subdivision has the same underlying set and every new simplex is contained in an old cell.

contents.name: 2.6–2.8(5), pp.13–15; Appendix to Chapter 2 pp.27–30 — adapted subclaim: Intersections of finite linear complexes form a convex cell complex
contents.support: If two finite linear simplicial complexes have the same underlying polyhedron, their nonempty intersections, with all faces, form a finite convex cell complex refining both. Each cell has finitely many faces and a relative interior point; its proper faces cover its boundary.

contents.name: 2.7(6), 2.9, pp.14–16; Appendix pp.29–30 — adapted subclaim: Finite convex cell complexes admit compatible triangulations
contents.support: Any finite convex cell complex has a simplicial triangulation obtained by choosing one relative interior point in each nonempty cell and coning its already triangulated boundary in increasing dimension.

contents.name: 2.8(5), 2.9 and 2.12, pp.15–16 — adapted subclaim: Two finite linear subdivisions have a common simplicial refinement
contents.support: Two finite linear subdivisions of a fixed finite Euclidean simplicial complex have a common finite simplicial refinement.
